unscoreable_emissions.reason: The bundled sections (ORC 101.70-.79; 121.60-.69; 101.90-.99) define 'legislative agent' qualitatively (main purpose/time) and require registration within 10 days of engagement, but they do not set any dollar compensation threshold for when registration is required.
The bundled statute text requires registration based on being a 'legislative agent' engaged to actively advocate, but does not establish any expenditure-dollar trigger for registration.

Although 'legislative agent' is defined as engaged 'during at least a portion of the individual's time' to actively advocate 'as one of the individual's main purposes,' the statute provides no quantitative time/percent threshold.

Expenditure statements require itemization for most expenditures and separately impose a $50 calendar-year threshold only for meals/food-and-beverages (ORC 101.73(B)(3)), but the compendium cell asks for a general itemization de minimis threshold; the statute does not provide a single general dollar threshold applicable to itemization beyond this category-specific rule.

The statute requires filing expenditure/financial-transaction statements with each updated registration statement (ORC 101.72(B); 101.73(A); 101.74(A)-(B)) and does not provide a general de minimis dollar amount below which filing is not required (aside from category-specific reporting rules for meals in ORC 101.73(B)(3)).

The bundled provisions contain no quantitative time-percentage threshold for filing expenditure/financial transaction statements; filing is tied to registration/engagement and reporting periods, not time spent lobbying.
